[CheckList](https://aclanthology.org/2020.acl-main.442.pdf) organizes behavioral tests into minimum functionality, invariance, and directional expectations; [contrast sets](https://aclanthology.org/2020.findings-emnlp.117/) use small, meaningful edits to expose local decision failures. Suggested recommendation adaptation: pair candidates differing in one explicit specification, distinguish near-identical listings from materially different editions or models, and test robustness to harmless title paraphrases. These are proposed diagnostic applications, not established recommendation benchmarks. A specification difference alone does not establish a user requirement or incompatibility.

[FEVER](https://aclanthology.org/N18-1074/) provides an auditable annotation pattern: supported, refuted, or insufficient information, with evidence sentences for supported/refuted judgments; reported Fleiss’ κ was 0.6841. Adapt this to rejection claims using exact title/description spans, item IDs, and relevant history entries. Double-annotate a sample; report label agreement, evidence-span agreement, adjudicated disagreements, and abstention coverage separately. Missing specifications should trigger insufficient information, rather than inferred conflicts; textual similarity should support a near-duplicate flag, not an ownership claim.

Recency deserves a separate diagnostic axis: [document-recommendation research](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/understanding-user-behavior-for-document-recommendation/) found recency associated with interaction, without establishing a universal preference for recent matches. Compare candidates matching recent histories versus broader historical themes, recording timestamps and textual evidence; treat preference direction as unknown. Recommendation research also distinguishes [explanation faithfulness from scrutability](https://doi.org/10.1145/3605357): a plausible text-grounded rationale need not explain the model’s actual computation. These probes can flag observable conflicts, redundancy, or weak grounding; they cannot establish ownership, actual compatibility, current intent, or willingness to choose.
